title: The Meaning of Bank Correspondence
body: Any communication with a bank should be in a simple style, precise language, and in a prescribed format. Secrecy must be maintained since it deals with money matters. Letters to banks are broadly divided into two categories: Request Letters and Complaint Letters.

title: Golden Rule of Banking Letters
body: Always mention your Account Number and the Type of Account (Savings or Current) clearly at the top of your letter. Without this, the bank cannot process your request!

title: Request Letters
body: Sometimes, you need something specific from the bank. For example, if you want to study abroad, you might need an Educational Loan. If you lost your ATM card, you must immediately ask the bank to block it. These are all types of 'Request Letters'.

title: Opening an Account
body: Many people think they have to write a formal letter to open an account. In reality, normally no letter is written! You just fill in a prescribed form provided by the bank and submit KYC documents.

title: Example: Stopping Payment of a Cheque
body: Imagine you issued a cheque of Rs. 10,000 to a supplier, but the cheque gets lost in transit. You must write a 'Stop Payment' request letter immediately, mentioning the Cheque Number, Date, Amount, and the name of the payee to prevent fraud.

title: Explain bank correspondence in brief.
body: Bank correspondence refers to the written communication between a customer and a bank. It must be precise, maintain financial secrecy, clearly state the account details, and properly write amounts in figures and words. It generally involves request letters and complaint letters.

title: Chapter Summary
body: In this chapter, we learned that banks are integral to commerce. Communication with banks must be precise, professional, and secure. We write Request Letters for services like loans, overdrafts, and blocking cards. We write Complaint Letters for issues like passbook errors, wrongful cheque dishonour, or rude behaviour. Always remember to include your account number and type!
